description: Remembers the git HEAD at the start of a session, and takes git snapshots of the working tree at each prompt and answer (a temporary index and refs/coders-talk/<session>; your branch, index and files are not touched), so /coders-talk:build can show which code each turn changed and what you changed by hand. When auto mode is on for this computer (/coders-talk:auto), sends the session in the background while it runs (every five minutes of work, checked after each answer and, without holding the agent up, after each tool call), when it ends, and at the next start if it never said it ended; otherwise sends nothing. Once per session, when the agent used Builds from the Coders Talk library and the session changed code, the Stop hook shows you a line suggesting to share it (it sends nothing; CODERS_TALK_NUDGE=0 turns it off). In a repository with your team's rules (coders-talk use --team), the SessionStart hook says in one line when the team changed them, and checks the site for that in the background at most every six hours (it never rewrites the block). It also adds your Coders Talk rules to the session's context: the ones for every session at its start, and a stack's rules with the prompt they matter for (matched on this computer: the prompt goes nowhere) (and your team's in its repositories, when the team turns that on), from what a background fetch kept at most an hour ago; nothing is written into the repository, and `coders-talk rules off` stops it.
